author: Aaronjacobs000
notes: Zoom Contact Center operation logs and voice call logs, polled from the Zoom Contact Center API by the example bridge in bridges/zoom-report-logs (set ZOOM_REPORTS to cc_operation_logs,cc_voice_calls) and posted to HTTP Ingest. Use a Server-to-Server OAuth app with only contact_center:read:operation_logs:admin and contact_center:read:voice_call_log:admin. The bridge puts "zoom_record" first (cc_operation or cc_voice_call) and adds account_id. Operation logs go to CloudAudit with the action as the event name, the category as the event type, the operator as the user, the object as the resource and operation_log_id as the event ID. Unmask, Download, Listen and Export read customer data or recordings, so they are read-only data events; every other action is a management event. Operation logs carry no IP address. Voice calls fit no schema, so they stay in Generic through the parent, with the engagement ID as the event ID and the call's start as the event time; the bridge asks for UTC, so their times end in +00:00. Agent IP and SBC fields appear only once Zoom Support turns on a flag for the account. Zoom documents the operation log fields, its action list and one example (Account, Create, "Add Flows: [inbox-voicemail]"); the categories, objects and details in the samples are made up in that shape, since Zoom's category table wasn't reachable. Voice call samples follow the response in Zoom's reference with made-up values. The child, combined with the parent into one parser, passed Run Test in a lab tenant on 2026-10-22 (63 of 63 fields matched the emulator in each of 3 runs), and the parent's confirm string picked the same records there. The child also passed Run Test as a separate parser under its parent (54 of 54 fields, each line taken in 5 of 5 runs), and the parent alone matched every voice call record. No built-in parser claimed these records in 3 runs.
